title: Remittances and bribery in Africa
publisher: In Konte and Mbaye (eds), Migration, Remittances, and Sustainable Development in Africa, Routledge, ch. 10, 179–198
summary: Using Afrobarometer surveys, the chapter finds that remittance receivers are more prone to bribe payment than non-receivers. Individuals in countries with higher remittances as a share of GDP are also more likely to pay bribes, in line with an income channel.
keyFindings: Remittance receivers are more prone to paying bribes than non-receivers.
People in countries with higher remittances as a share of GDP are more likely to pay bribes.
methods: Afrobarometer survey data for African countries.
